system.name: DepMGNN
system.one_liner: Video-based depression assessment with a matrixial graph whose nodes hold whole 2D facial feature maps, processed by a matrixial graph neural network.

content.variant_note: three sibling pipelines in aligned columns (decision level, feature level, ours) plus a narrow second panel that contrasts a vector-based graph with the matrixial graph
content.argues: Matrixial graphs keep the spatial structure of frame-level feature maps that decision-level and feature-level fusion of vectors lose.
content.subject: Three video pipelines from face frames to clip-level prediction, and two toy graphs with vector versus matrix nodes and edges.

lessons.what_to_learn: Draw the baselines and the proposal as columns that share one skeleton so only the point where they differ changes, then repeat that difference in a small second panel at glyph level (slab versus feature map, single value versus matrix) with a one-line verdict under each.
lessons.suits: methods that change what is passed between stages (vector versus matrix, set versus graph), where a same-skeleton comparison plus a glyph-level contrast carries the point.

evidence: Our approach directly includes multi-scale 2D facial feature maps of each frame as a set of nodes
In existing graphs, each node can not only include a vector (or a single value)
Fig. 1 compares our approach with previous solutions.

summary: DepMGNN assesses depression from face videos of any length by building a matrixial graph whose nodes hold whole 2D facial feature maps and whose edges are matrices, then running a matrixial graph neural network over it. The figure has two numbered, purple-framed panels. Panel 1 puts three pipelines in aligned columns: decision-level and feature-level fusion, which reduce each frame to a vector before aggregating, and the proposed one, where multi-scale feature-map thumbnails become the nodes of a spatio-temporal matrixial graph processed by MGR(MGNN) and a prediction head. Panel 2 contrasts a vector-based graph with single-value edges against the matrixial graph with matrix nodes and edges. Film strips of real faces, dark-teal feature maps and a pale lavender-purple palette.

notes: Kinds extend the prior (side-by-side-contrast, model-anatomy) with concept-schematic for panel 2 (the toy graphs are a formal picture of the data structure). The acronyms MGL and MGR are not expanded in the context, and the four edge colours of the 4 by 4 graph are not keyed, so their roles are left open. Picture counts follow the digest (84 placed bitmaps: 64 feature-map layers plus small thumbnails); the face frames are assumed to be bitmaps. Panel 1 lists no sub-panels: its three columns are lanes.
